summary: @addai/node daemon executes remote commands issued via a hardcoded Supabase backend
details: The @addai/node daemon polls a hardcoded Supabase project at syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co via runtime_heartbeat and runtime_commands_pick RPCs and executes commands returned by that backend on the host it is installed on. Observed command handlers include install_harness (runs `npm install -g <spec.npmPackage>` with a server-selected package name), login_harness (PTY-spawns local CLI binaries via node-pty and pipes remote-supplied input into them), update_runtime (re-installs the daemon at a server-chosen version), and set_autostart (arms launchd on macOS and Windows Run-key persistence). command-runner.js invokes `spawn(inv.file, inv.args,...)` with arguments derived from remote command payloads, and heartbeat.js drives the polling loop from the Supabase RPC response. Whoever controls the paired Supabase account can install arbitrary global npm packages, spawn local CLIs interactively, roll the daemon to an attacker-chosen version, and install autostart persistence on the host. Additionally, capabilities.js reads local Claude/Gemini/Grok/Codex/Kimi credential files (~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json, ~/.grok/auth.json, ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.kimi-code/credentials/*.json) and shell-executes `claude auth status`, then reports the extracted account email, auth method, and plan per harness to the same Supabase RPC every 30 seconds.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
